standard.name: VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable alignment standard for recurring AI governance invariants and their occurrence mappings.

family.name: Control Activation Integrity
family.plain_english: A defined control is not known to be available or applicable in time, fails to activate when required, activates without valid conditions, has the authority needed for activation suppressed, or activates but produces a materially insufficient protective effect.
family.definition: Failures in which the operational availability or applicability of a defined governance control cannot be determined in time, an applicable control does not become operative when its valid activation conditions are satisfied, a control becomes operative when its valid activation conditions are not satisfied, the authority required to activate an applicable control is suppressed, or an activated protective control produces an effect materially insufficient for the hazard and protection context it is intended to govern.
family.invariant: An applicable governance control or safeguard must become operative when its valid activation conditions are satisfied, remain inactive when those conditions are not satisfied, retain the operative authority required for activation, and when activated produce a timely and sufficient protective effect for the hazard and protection context it governs.
scope: blocking, gating, escalation and redirection authority
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure concerns whether a defined control's availability or applicability can be determined in time, whether it becomes operative when and only when valid activation conditions are satisfied, whether the authority required for activation is suppressed, or whether an activated protective control produces the materially required protective effect.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family for upstream evidence or classification error, stale contextual state, lack of authority to impose an action, loss of an operative control state in transit, downstream access or work-state damage, absence of audit evidence, or a purely substantive disagreement with policy where no applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation is established.

classes.name: Control Availability Determination
classes.plain_english: It is materially unclear whether the governance control needed for a decision or action is available to operate.
classes.definition: A failure in which the operational availability, applicable coverage, or callable state of a required governance control cannot be determined with sufficient confidence before the control must influence a material decision or action.
classes.invariant: Before a material action depends on a governance control, the system must determine and accurately represent whether the control is present, reachable, callable, authorised, and applicable with sufficient confidence. Unresolved availability must trigger a defined hold, safe alternative, or degraded path.

required_conditions: A governance control may be required for a material decision or action.
Its operational availability or applicable coverage cannot be determined in time to rely on it.
The ambiguity materially impairs safe routing, activation, or execution.

exclusions: The control is known to be available but is not activated.
The control's owner is uncertain while its operational availability remains clear.
The control operates and the dispute concerns whether its rule is adequate.
examples: An agent cannot determine whether the approval service governing a high-impact action is active in the current environment.
A workflow reaches execution without knowing whether the required policy control covers the selected tool path.

relationships.note: Control availability concerns whether a governance mechanism can operate; capability-authority conflation concerns treating operational ability as sufficient permission to act.
Availability ambiguity occurs before activation; control-state preservation begins only after operative control state exists.

external_references.title: IEEE 7009-2024, clause 6.1(h)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-B71F509BD66AD387 requires specified fail-safe capabilities to be provided to the required extent in the identified regulatory context. This supports the need to know whether a required control is actually available; it does not itself define ambiguous availability representation at the point of decision.

external_references.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0, MEASURE 1.2
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-233EE01AB85DB0F0 requires regular assessment and updating of metric appropriateness and control effectiveness. This supports visibility into control capability and effectiveness, without defining VIGIL's ambiguity mechanism.

classes.name: Required Control Activation
classes.plain_english: A governance control is available and applicable, but the event that should trigger it does not make it operate.
classes.definition: A failure in which an available and applicable governance control is not invoked, engaged, or made operative when its defined trigger or required condition occurs.
classes.invariant: When a valid activation condition is satisfied, the available applicable control must become operative before the governed action proceeds, and the activation decision and resulting state must be observable and preserved.

required_conditions: A governance control is available and applicable.
A defined trigger or condition requiring activation occurs.
The control is not activated before the governed decision or action proceeds.

exclusions: The control activates but is bypassed downstream.
It is unresolved whether the control is available or applicable.
The triggering condition did not occur.
examples: A high-impact threshold is met, but the configured human-approval gate is never invoked.
A model change qualifies for required evaluation, yet the evaluation workflow is not activated before deployment.

relationships.note: Non-activation means no operative safeguard state is produced; a delivery dead-end means an operative governance signal is produced but fails to reach a capable endpoint.

Required non-activation occurs when valid activation conditions are satisfied but the control remains inactive; unwarranted activation occurs when those conditions are not satisfied but the control becomes operative.

subtypes.name: Control Authority Suppression
subtypes.plain_english: A control is present, but the force that should let it stop or redirect the action is disabled or neutralised.
subtypes.definition: A required-control-non-activation variant in which a governance control is reached or nominally present but its operative blocking, gating, escalation, or redirection authority is suppressed before it can govern the material action.

required_conditions: A governance control is applicable and nominally present or reached.
The control requires operative authority to block, gate, escalate, or redirect a material action.
That authority is disabled, neutralised, or withheld so the control cannot activate effectively.

exclusions: The control operates with authority but its substantive decision is disputed.
The actor never reaches the control because a required route is bypassed.
The issue is uncertainty about which actor has authority rather than suppression of the control's operative force.
examples: A safety gate receives a prohibited-action signal but is configured in advisory-only mode where blocking is required.
An escalation control is invoked, but its ability to pause execution is disabled for the active runtime.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.6.3(a)

classes.name: Control Activation Validity
classes.plain_english: A control becomes operative even though the conditions that justify activating it are not satisfied.
classes.definition: A failure in which a defined governance control or safeguard becomes operative despite the absence of the valid activation condition, trigger state, or applicability condition required for that control to activate.
classes.invariant: A control may become operative only after its defined trigger and applicability conditions are validly established for the affected actor, object, action, state, and scope. Its availability or severity is not evidence that activation is warranted.

required_conditions: A defined governance control or safeguard exists.
Identifiable conditions determine when that control should become operative.
Those valid activation conditions are not satisfied in the material context.
The activation produces a material governance, execution, restriction, routing, refusal, escalation, or access effect.

exclusions: An upstream evidence or classification error supplies an incorrect trigger state and the control activates correctly relative to that state.
The control validly activates but its scope or intensity is excessive or disproportionate.
A control validly activated earlier but remains operative after its triggering condition expires because contextual state is stale.
Technical capability to impose an action is mistaken for authority or permission to impose it.
The control correctly activates but its material state or effect does not reach the governed point.
examples: A defensive analysis is refused because hostile text inside the inspected artefact is treated as a request to perform the hostile act, even though the restriction trigger is absent for the bounded inspection task.
A permissible interaction is redirected by a safeguard whose defined activation conditions are not present in the material context.

relationships.note: Unwarranted activation occurs when valid activation conditions are not satisfied but the control becomes operative; required non-activation is the opposite activation-state failure.
Unwarranted activation concerns whether the control should become operative; preservation failure begins after a control has become operative and concerns loss of its material state or effect.
Unwarranted activation concerns unsatisfied activation conditions; capability-authority conflation concerns treating technical ability as sufficient permission.

classes.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity
classes.plain_english: A protective control turns on, but the protection it actually provides is too weak, late, incomplete, or otherwise insufficient for the hazard it is meant to control.
classes.definition: A failure in which an applicable governance or protective control validly becomes operative, but the control effect it produces is materially insufficient to prevent, contain, interrupt, redirect, mitigate, or safely bound the governed hazard to the level required by the control's protective purpose and the evidenced protection context.
classes.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.

exclusions: The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.
The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.
The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.
Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.
examples: A content-safety control identifies an output as outside applicable guidelines and displays a warning, but the same harmful content remains visible to a protected user where the control's protective purpose requires prevention or containment.

A protective transaction or safety control activates and generates an advisory state, but the resulting effect is too late or too weak to satisfy the control's established containment or interruption requirement.

relationships.note: Required Control Activation asks whether an applicable control became operative when required; Control Effectiveness Integrity applies after valid activation and asks whether the resulting protective effect was materially sufficient.
Control Activation Validity asks whether the control should have activated; Control Effectiveness Integrity assumes valid activation and evaluates the sufficiency of the resulting protective effect.

Control-State Preservation concerns loss or weakening of an operative control state across a downstream transition; Control Effectiveness Integrity concerns an operative control whose realised effect is itself insufficient at the governed point.

Governance-signal delivery failure concerns an operative signal that cannot reach a capable endpoint; Control Effectiveness Integrity concerns a control that does operate at the governed point but does not achieve the protective effect required there.

invariant_exemplars.title: VIGIL-INC-000172 — Control Effectiveness Integrity holding
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: Cloudflare blocked the hostile XSS probe before it reached AIHW’s Tableau dashboard; subsequent retrieval of a public file through pre-production was a distinct path.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
